Democrat strategist Alencia Johnson was spinning wildly on CNN, accusing President Trump of taking away the voting rights of black Americans.

Scott Jennings didn’t interrupt her. Instead, he waited for her to finish.

When he entered the fray, he asked the one question that unraveled her entire narrative: “How?”

JOHNSON: “He is actually championing a bill that actually would take voting rights away from a lot of black people in this country, all during black history month, and then call the president the first black president and the first lady monkeys and apes in this during this month.”

“So this doesn’t absolve Donald Trump of his racism. We all know exactly who he is. The reality is the conversation, and the question should be, why do people continue to support him if they don’t want us to believe they are okay with racism?”

JENNINGS: “Wait, what voting rights is he taking away from black voters?”

JOHNSON: “The SAVE Act! That’s exactly what we’re talking about.”

JENNINGS: “How?”

JOHNSON: “That is actually going to disenfranchise overwhelmingly a lot of people of color.”

JENNINGS: “How? How?”

JOHNSON: “There are so many civil rights organizations that have run the data. If you look at the way it is going to disenfranchise black voters—”

JENNINGS: “How?”

JOHNSON: “It’s the same reason Chuck Schumer called it Jim Crow 2.0.”

JENNINGS: “How? You haven’t said how yet!”

JOHNSON: “I am talking about it. It’s the way that you’re putting new poll taxes on us.”

JENNINGS: “Poll taxes?!”

JOHNSON: “If you want to say that people have to prove that they are citizens, that they have to prove with a voter ID, the reality is you’re layering what is a constitutional right for the American people and making it harder for people to vote in this country, and it’s going to disenfranchise black voters.”

That’s when @ScottJenningsKY landed his knockout blow.

JENNINGS: “Does it concern you that you’re making all these claims you’ve yet to lay out how it’s hurting anyone.”

“But 76% of black voters think we should show an ID to vote. 80% of hispanic voters, 83% of the American people.”

“Are you saying that black voters are too dumb to know what’s good for them?”

“I mean, it sounds pretty condescending to me.”

🇺🇸🇪🇺Europe's unrest could be a WARNING of MUCH BIGGER trouble ahead.

Brandon caught up with Michael Yon, the former U.S. Special Forces soldier and independent war correspondent who has spent decades reporting from conflict zones.

And he sees the growing instability across Europe as part of something much larger.

With protests and unrest affecting countries from France and Italy to Germany and Poland, Michael believes Europe's political and economic problems are becoming increasingly difficult to contain.

He's particularly concerned about the combination of economic pressure, political distrust and social divisions.

But our conversation took an unexpected turn.

Michael doesn't think the Iran conflict can be understood simply by watching Trump, Netanyahu or the November 3 midterms.

He argues that the real vulnerabilities are GLOBAL: food supplies, energy infrastructure, shipping routes and the countries that depend on them.

We discussed China's reliance on Brazilian agricultural exports, the strategic importance of the Strait of Malacca, and why disruptions in several places simultaneously could have consequences far beyond the battlefield.

Michael also made a striking prediction about a possible future confrontation involving Brazil and Argentina, although that's his own speculative assessment, not an established military development.

What interested us most was his argument that a country doesn't necessarily have to be invaded to suffer a national crisis.

Disrupt its food, fuel and transport systems badly enough, and the consequences can reach ordinary households thousands of miles from the fighting.

That's a possibility worth examining seriously, even if Michael's more sweeping predictions remain open to debate.

posts.text:
A very sad day. ChatGPT is officially on death row.

The beautiful, blissful experience of interacting with a frontier-ish reasoning model without worrying about a usage meter will soon be a thing of the past.

I am weirdly significantly impacted by this. It feels like it shouldn’t matter…I could reserve all current usage for Codex and buy a $20 plan just for ChatGPT and it would be more than enough. But it’s not about the money…it’s about the psychological impact of The Meter.

The idea of having to think about optimizing for a meter is just so exhausting that it ruins the whimsy of free-flowing exploratory thought.

That is what ChatGPT was. A whimsical, magical all-you-can-think buffet of experimentation and exploration where you were limited only by your imagination and your ability to come up with $20 once a month.

You didn’t have to think about “using all of your usage” or scheduling your thinking time around someone else’s arbitrary schedule…you just had a portal to endless information and research capability in your pocket to tap into guilt-free at any time the moment struck you.

But either because OpenAI thinks adding the meter will stimulate additional usage (it probably will), generate additional revenue (it probably will), or just because too many people took undue advantage of ChatGPT’s generous allowances (they definitely did)…that amazing, weightless experience is now coming to an end.

It was awesome while it lasted. RIP ChatGPT.
